title: Report precision and recall
concept: What do precision and recall measure?
summary: Precision asks what share of the cases the model flagged were right. Recall asks what share of the cases that mattered it found. They move in opposite directions as a threshold changes, so a single accuracy number hides the trade a product actually makes.
example: 42 correct flags, 8 wrong flags and 10 missed cases give precision 0.84 and recall about 0.81.
takeaway: Each metric has its own denominator, and a denominator of zero means the question was never asked rather than that the model scored zero.
instruction: Given nonnegative integers truePositives, falsePositives and falseNegatives, return {precision, recall, f1} rounded to four decimal places. Precision is truePositives over flagged cases, recall is truePositives over cases that mattered, and f1 is 2 x truePositives over (2 x truePositives + falsePositives + falseNegatives). Return 0 for any metric whose denominator is 0.
hint: Compute each metric from the unrounded counts and round only what you return. Guard each denominator separately.
